chunks: When a woman gives birth, she refrains from salat (prayer) for ten days, unless she becomes pure before that. If the blood continues with her, she leaves salat (prayer) for up to eighteen days.
Because Asmāʾ bint ʿUmays had postnatal bleeding with Muḥammad ibn Abī Bakr during the Farewell Pilgrimage, and the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله instructed her to refrain for eighteen days.

key_terms.تَطْهُرَ: to become pure, meaning the bleeding stops
key_terms.حَجَّةِ ٱلْوَدَاعِ: the Farewell Pilgrimage, the historical setting of the report
key_terms.رَسُولُ ٱللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, who gave the instruction
key_terms.ٱلصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), which is left during nifas
key_terms.ٱلْمَرْأَةُ: the woman giving birth who is subject to the ruling

ai.seo_question: How long does a woman refrain from salat (prayer) after childbirth according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on nifas, the postpartum bleeding period, stating that a woman refrains from salat (prayer) for ten days unless purity returns earlier. If the bleeding continues, the ruling extends up to eighteen days, supported by the precedent of Asmāʾ bint ʿUmays during the Farewell Pilgrimage.
